question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

VV, QP, LJ, GD, BX, ?, RL, MF
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. WR.

GIVEN

• VV, QP, LJ, GD, BX, ?, RL, MF

SOLUTION

• First letters: V(22), Q(17), L(12), G(7), B(2), ?, R(18), M(13) — each step −5 (mod 26): 2−5 = 23 = W.

• Second letters: V(22), P(16), J(10), D(4), X(24), ?, L(12), F(6) — each step −6 (mod 26): 24−6 = 18 = R.

• Missing term = WR.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Split every cluster into two independent letter-ladders; here one drops by 5, the other by 6. Feed the previous term to get W and R instantly.

NOTE

• For two-letter series, always separate 1st and 2nd letters and check their position gaps (A=1 … Z=26) using mod-26 wrap-around.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

XY, VV, TR, ?, PG, NZ, LR, JI
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. RM.

GIVEN

• XY, VV, TR, ?, PG, NZ, LR, JI

SOLUTION

• First letters: X(24), V(22), T(20), ?, P(16)… — constant −2: 20−2 = 18 = R.

• Second letters: Y(25), V(22), R(18), ?, G(7), Z(26), R(18), I(9) — gaps −3, −4, −5, −6, −7, −8, −9. From R(18): 18−5 = 13 = M.

• Missing term = RM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter is a plain −2 ladder → R. That alone leaves only RJ and RM; the widening −gap on the second letter fixes M.

NOTE

• When simple constant differences fail on the second letter, test an increasing/decreasing difference pattern (−3, −4, −5 …).

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

PT : LG :: LY : HB :: HA : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. DZ.

GIVEN

• PT : LG :: LY : HB :: HA : ?

SOLUTION

• 1st letter: subtract 4 → P(16)−4 = L, L(12)−4 = H. So H(8)−4 = D.

• 2nd letter: replace by its opposite (27−x) → T(20)→G(7), Y(25)→B(2). So A(1)→27−1 = 26 = Z.

• Therefore HA → DZ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Two rules: first letter −4, second letter mirror (A↔Z). Apply to H and A → D and Z.

NOTE

• Opposite letter pairs sum to 27 (A+Z, B+Y, C+X …); memorising this makes mirror-type clusters one-step.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(IP, CJ, VC)

(GR, AL, TE)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (KM, EG, XZ).

GIVEN

• (IP, CJ, VC) → each pair second = first +7 (I+7=P, C+7=J, V+7=C mod 26).

• (GR, AL, TE) → each pair second = first +11.

SOLUTION

• Rule: inside a valid set, all three clusters share the SAME internal gap.

• (KM, EG, XZ): K+2=M, E+2=G, X+2=Z → constant +2 for all three. ✓

• Others fail: (EF +1, YX −1…), (SU +2, MI −4…), (AF +5, UU 0…).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just compute the gap in each cluster of an option; keep the option where all gaps are equal.

NOTE

• Odd-set/analogy questions with grouped clusters almost always hinge on a common intra-cluster difference.

question: What will be the sum of number of Thursdays, Fridays and Sundays in November 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• Month = November 2025 (30 days).

SOLUTION

• 1 November 2025 is a Saturday.

• 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 extra days; the 2 extra days are Sat (1st) and Sun (2nd).

• So Saturday and Sunday come 5 times; every other day 4 times.

• Thursdays = 4, Fridays = 4, Sundays = 5 → 4 + 4 + 5 = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In a 30-day month only the first 2 weekdays repeat 5 times; check whether Thu/Fri/Sun fall among them.

NOTE

• 30 days → two days occur 5×; 31 days → three days occur 5×; 28 days → all occur exactly 4×.

question: The calendar for the year 2007 will be the same as which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2018.

GIVEN

• Base year = 2007 (an ordinary/non-leap year).

SOLUTION

• A repeating calendar needs the total odd days from the base year onward to be a multiple of 7, and the target must also be an ordinary year.

• Odd days: 2007→1, 2008→2, 2009→1, 2010→1, 2011→1, 2012→2, 2013→1, 2014→1, 2015→1, 2016→2, 2017→1 = 14 ≡ 0 (mod 7).

• So the calendar repeats in 2018.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• An ordinary year’s calendar usually repeats after 6 or 11 years; here the running odd-day total first clears at +11 → 2018.

NOTE

• Ordinary year = 1 odd day, leap year = 2 odd days; add them up until the sum is divisible by 7.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with triangle (top), square (middle), rectangle (bottom).

GIVEN

• 1st box (○, −, +) → 2nd box (+, ○, −).

• 3rd box (□, small-rectangle, △) → ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: the bottom symbol moves to the top and the other two shift down by one place (downward cyclic rotation).

• Apply to (□, rectangle, △): bottom △ goes to top → (△, □, rectangle).

• This matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Read the stack top-to-bottom and just cycle it down by one step (last element jumps to first).

NOTE

• In symbol-stack analogies, first test simple cyclic shifts (up or down by one) before looking for reflection or replacement.

question:
Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.

13254 : 31245 :: 64897 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 46879.

GIVEN

• 13254 : 31245 :: 64897 : ?

SOLUTION

• Compare 13254 → 31245: swap the 1st and 2nd digits, keep the 3rd digit, swap the 4th and 5th digits.

• 1 3 2 5 4 → 3 1 2 4 5. ✓

• Apply to 6 4 8 9 7: swap first two (4 6), keep 8, swap last two (7 9) → 4 6 8 7 9 = 46879.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the middle digit; interchange the outer pairs (positions 1↔2 and 4↔5).

NOTE

• For number-cluster analogies, first check for positional rearrangement (swaps/reversals) before arithmetic operations.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AK160 : CO100 :: BP240 : ? :: CQ180 : EU120
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. DT180.

GIVEN

• AK160 : CO100 :: BP240 : ? :: CQ180 : EU120

SOLUTION

• Check AK160 → CO100: A(+2)=C, K(+4)=O, 160−60 = 100.

• Check CQ180 → EU120: C(+2)=E, Q(+4)=U, 180−60 = 120. Same rule.

• Apply to BP240: B(+2)=D, P(+4)=T, 240−60 = 180 → DT180.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Rule = 1st letter +2, 2nd letter +4, number −60. Plug BP240 straight in.

NOTE

• Confirm a proposed rule on BOTH given pairs before applying it to the unknown pair.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AMR10 : CPM99 :: BKP13 : DNK168 :: RTW25 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. TWR624.

GIVEN

• AMR10 : CPM99 :: BKP13 : DNK168 :: RTW25 : ?

SOLUTION

• Letters: 1st +2, 2nd +3, 3rd −5. Check A+2=C, M+3=P, R−5=M ✓; B+2=D, K+3=N, P−5=K ✓.

• Number: n² − 1. Check 10²−1 = 99 ✓; 13²−1 = 168 ✓.

• Apply to RTW25: R+2=T, T+3=W, W−5=R, 25²−1 = 624 → TWR624.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters shift +2/+3/−5; number becomes (square − 1). For 25 → 625−1 = 624.

NOTE

• Numbers like 99, 168, 624 are n²−1 (100−1, 169−1, 625−1); spotting near-perfect-squares speeds these up.

question: In a certain coded language 'DUDS' is coded as 'EWCO' and 'SLUM' is coded as 'TNTI'. How will 'MUCH' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. NWBD.

GIVEN

• DUDS → EWCO and SLUM → TNTI.

SOLUTION

• Letter shifts (position by position): +1, +2, −1, −4.

• Verify DUDS: D+1=E, U+2=W, D−1=C, S−4=O = EWCO ✓. SLUM: S+1=T, L+2=N, U−1=T, M−4=I = TNTI ✓.

• MUCH: M+1=N, U+2=W, C−1=B, H−4=D → NWBD.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply the fixed offset pattern +1, +2, −1, −4 to M, U, C, H.

NOTE

• In positional coding, find one consistent shift per letter-position using both given words, then apply to the query word.

question: In a certain code language, 'create brings girls cares' is coded as 'nlg tmf nkf khk', 'every girls fear above' is coded as 'nmh tmf toj wip' and 'blood fear cover roads' is coded as 'qnd ifl zhd wip'. How will 'girls fear' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. tmf wip.

GIVEN

• create brings girls cares = nlg tmf nkf khk

• every girls fear above = nmh tmf toj wip

• blood fear cover roads = qnd ifl zhd wip

SOLUTION

• 'girls' is common to lines 1 & 2 → common code tmf.

• 'fear' is common to lines 2 & 3 → common code wip.

• So 'girls fear' = tmf wip.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the repeated word across two sentences to the repeated code word.

NOTE

• In message/substitution coding, intersect the word-sets and code-sets of two lines sharing a word to lock that word’s code.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

ZR150, WW244, TB338, QG432, NL526, JR621
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. JR621.

GIVEN

• ZR150, WW244, TB338, QG432, NL526, JR621

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: Z(26), W(23), T(20), Q(17), N(14), … → −3 each, next should be K(11), not J.

• 2nd letters: R(18), W(23), B(2), G(7), L(12), … → +5 each, next should be Q(17), not R.

• Numbers: 150, 244, 338, 432, 526, … → +94 each, next should be 620, not 621.

• So the correct 6th term is KQ620; the given JR621 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Extend all three ladders (−3 letters, +5 letters, +94 numbers); JR621 breaks every one.

NOTE

• Wrong-term problems: track each component (letters and number) separately and flag the term that deviates.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

NOT108, STY216, XYD324, ?, HIN540
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. CDI432.

GIVEN

• NOT108, STY216, XYD324, ?, HIN540

SOLUTION

• Each letter advances +5 (mod 26). 1st: N(14), S(19), X(24), C(29≡3), H(34≡8) → C.

• 2nd: O(15), T(20), Y(25), D(30≡4), I(35≡9) → D.

• 3rd: T(20), Y(25), D(30≡4), I(35≡9), N(40≡14) → I.

• Numbers: 108, 216, 324, 432, 540 (+108 each) → 432.

• Missing term = CDI432.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Every letter jumps +5 and the number jumps +108; slot the 4th term between 324 and 540 → 432, letters C-D-I.

NOTE

• Use mod-26 wrap (e.g. 29→3=C) when a +5 shift crosses Z.

question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 5 PM and 6 PM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 130 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5:04.

GIVEN

• Time between 5 PM and 6 PM; required angle = 130°.

SOLUTION

• Angle = |30H − 5.5M|. At H = 5: |150 − 5.5M| = 130.

• Case 150 − 5.5M = 130 → 5.5M = 20 → M ≈ 3.6 min ≈ 5:04.

• (Other case gives M ≈ 51, i.e. ~5:51, not in the options.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Use angle = |30H − 5.5M|; solve for M with the smaller root → about 4 minutes past 5.

NOTE

• Minute hand moves 5.5° per minute relative to the hour hand; each target angle gives two times in the hour.

question: A clock is 5 minutes fast at 11:30 AM and 11 minutes fast at 11:30 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1:30.

GIVEN

• +5 min fast at 11:30 AM, +11 min fast at 11:30 PM (12-hour gap).

SOLUTION

• Gain in 12 hours = 11 − 5 = 6 min → rate = 0.5 min per hour.

• At 11:30 AM it is 5 min ahead; it was exactly correct 5 ÷ 0.5 = 10 hours earlier.

• 11:30 AM − 10 hours = 1:30 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Rate 0.5 min/hr; to erase a 5-min lead go back 10 hours from 11:30 AM → 1:30 AM.

NOTE

• Correct-time instant = reference time minus (current error ÷ gain-rate), moving toward zero error.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the upright bucket-shape with the arrow pointing downward.

GIVEN

• Four figures of a bucket/trapezoid with an attached arrow, rotating step by step, then ?

SOLUTION

• The whole figure rotates 45° clockwise at each step.

• Continuing the rotation from the 4th figure, the bucket returns to an upright position with the arrow pointing straight down.

• This matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Track only the arrow direction; it turns 45° clockwise each time and lands pointing down.

NOTE

• For single-object figure series, fix on one marker (arrow/pointer) and measure its constant rotation per step.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the figure with the small triangle at the bottom-left corner.

GIVEN

• A quartered circle (two black quarters) with a small triangle moving around the corners of the box.

SOLUTION

• The triangle shifts one corner per step: bottom-left → bottom-right → top-right → top-left → back to bottom-left.

• After the 4th figure (triangle at top-left), the 5th must place the triangle again at the bottom-left, with the same shaded circle.

• This matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The corner-triangle cycles through the four corners; after top-left it returns to bottom-left.

NOTE

• When a small marker travels around corners, treat it as a 4-step cycle and just find the next corner in sequence.

question: Difference between the present ages of A and B is 10 years. 3 years ago from present, the ratio of ages of A and B is 22 : 17. What is the present age of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 37 years.

GIVEN

• Present age difference (A − B) = 10 years.

• 3 years ago, A : B = 22 : 17.

SOLUTION

• 3 years ago let A = 22x, B = 17x. The difference stays 10: 22x − 17x = 5x = 10 → x = 2.

• B, 3 years ago = 17 × 2 = 34 → present B = 34 + 3 = 37 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference of ratio parts (22−17 = 5) equals the constant age gap 10 → 1 part = 2 years; B = 17×2 + 3 = 37.

NOTE

• Age difference never changes with time, so equate it to the difference of the ratio parts to find the multiplier.

question: Father's age 10 years ago from present was 2 times of the age of his son 8 years ago from present. Son's age after 3 years from present is 32 years. What is the sum of present ages of father and son?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 81 years.

GIVEN

• Father (10 years ago) = 2 × Son (8 years ago).

• Son’s age after 3 years = 32.

SOLUTION

• Present son = 32 − 3 = 29. Son 8 years ago = 29 − 8 = 21.

• Father 10 years ago = 2 × 21 = 42 → present father = 42 + 10 = 52.

• Sum of present ages = 52 + 29 = 81 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Work son first (29), back to 21, double to 42, add 10 → father 52; total 81.

NOTE

• Always convert every ‘years ago/after’ statement to present age before summing.
